title: Caribou Walk Over 2,000 Miles a Year, the Longest Land Migration

scenes.text: No land mammal travels as far as this one.
Some caribou herds in Alaska and Canada walk more than two thousand miles every year.
That's the longest land migration of any mammal.
They cross tundra, rivers and mountains, following the seasons to find food.
The Porcupine herd alone has about two hundred thousand animals.
Two hundred thousand animals, walking two thousand miles. Every single year.

description:
Some caribou herds walk more than 2,000 miles a year, the longest land migration of any mammal.
The Porcupine herd, which moves through Alaska and Canada, numbered about 218,000 animals as of 2017.
Could you walk 2,000 miles? Tell us below.
